reviewed_scope.companions: Lifecycle/retrieval/migration prose was still being authored and was not used as an implicit fix for missing dictionary/schema constraints.

findings.title: The ownership promise is not yet an enforceable relationship design.
findings.issue: The dictionary says all private FKs use composite database constraints, but most target entities do not declare unique(id,owner_id). Private-to-mixed links are described as same owner OR public, which an equality composite FK cannot express. Public Product/TermsDocument links to mixed EvidenceSpan/DocumentRevision also need an explicit public-target restriction. NULL owner values need deliberate handling; they must not bypass existence/scope checks. Staff approver/reviewer actor references cannot be forced to equal the customer owner.
findings.required_revision: Specify a relationship-by-relationship access matrix: owner-bound, public-only, public-or-owner, and independently authorized actor. Declare required composite target keys and the exact trigger/check strategy for nullable mixed targets, with update/delete enforcement and actor exceptions. Include public corpus rejection of private sources.

findings.title: Same owner does not enforce the required conversation, revision or contract lineage.
findings.issue: Several fields require same conversation/revision/person/predicate or member scope, while physical child rows contain only FK IDs and owner_id. SnapshotFact one accepted scalar value per subject/predicate depends on FactAssertion fields in another row. These cannot be enforced by an ordinary CHECK over the child row or by owner equality alone. Supersession currently says same owner/subject/predicate, without explicitly requiring the intended conversation lineage.
findings.required_revision: Provide exact composite keys or deferred constraint triggers for conversation/revision/subject lineage and sealed snapshot membership. Define scalar versus multivalued predicates and a concrete invariant for accepted snapshot facts. Validate cyclic insertion and erasure transitions; do not rely on ORM save hooks for bulk import correctness.

findings.title: Native Django authentication mapping remains internally incomplete.
findings.issue: AuthPermission declares app_label/model_name as fields although native django.contrib.auth.Permission stores content_type_id referencing ContentType; no ContentType entity/mapping is present. AccountGroup/AccountPermission use logical owner_id but native joins use user_id; their IDs are BigAutoField in the pilot accounts app, whereas the proposal says integer. Native auth Group/Permission use AutoField. Native admin LogEntry/content-type history is not explicitly accounted for. LegacyMapping.target_id is UUID-only and cannot directly identify native integer/string targets.
findings.required_revision: Distinguish logical projections from physical native fields. Include native ContentType plus Permission.content_type_id, explicit user_id aliases for account joins and correct native ID widths. Identify retained admin/session tables and a target-key representation for UUID, integer and session-string identities. Preserve encoded passwords and existing sessions without a custom auth-table substitute.

findings.title: Ledger idempotency references an event key that does not exist.
findings.issue: UsageEntry promises idempotency via claim_line,kind,scope,event, but has no event_id or stable posting/idempotency key and no declared unique constraint implementing that combination. occurred_on is not an event identity. Repeating a worker/import or partial settlement can duplicate reserves, threshold use, cover consumption or payment. Nullable claim_line_id also permits legitimate non-claim postings requiring their own identity.
findings.required_revision: Add a stable posting/event identity with a concrete scoped unique constraint for all posting kinds. Specify how claim-line assessment revisions and source settlement events generate distinct postings, and how reversals are limited atomically. Define immutable assessment revision/current-selection semantics so usage cannot point ambiguously at repeated assessments.

findings.title: Selective medical-fact deletion has no complete typed target/dependency representation.
findings.issue: DeletionScopeV1 supports account, conversation, person or artifacts; Artifact.kind excludes fact assertions, messages, search chunks, processing outputs and model-response copies. The worked case requests deletion of one disclosure and its derived copies while retaining unrelated facts. Mapping it only to a fact_snapshot would either leave copies outside the graph or erase a broader snapshot. The generic immutable-artifact graph does not yet identify all physical copies whose erasure must be verified.
findings.required_revision: Specify an explicit assertion/content target and how its copied values are indexed through messages, snapshots, decisions, search chunks, model/worker payloads, exports and retention-managed stores. Keep lineage tombstones separate from erased payloads and prevent old workers or migrations from resurrecting erased data. Define a scoped receipt without retained medical values.

findings.title: No explicit conversation-context reuse authorization is represented.
findings.issue: The case requires a new conversation to prohibit reuse of old medical facts and later permit only explicitly scoped reuse. Conversation has no import/reuse policy, ConsentRecord purposes do not include cross-conversation reuse, and source_kind has no traceable authorized import. Same-owner checks alone cannot implement the user preference; copying old assertions into new ones would hide their origin.
findings.required_revision: Define the persisted no-reuse/default policy, a source-to-destination conversation grant or import event, scoped facts/persons and revocation behavior. Ensure retrieval, prompts and derived dependencies obey it. If the design forbids all cross-conversation reuse, state how an explicit later reuse request is handled rather than implicitly treating account ownership as permission.

findings.title: Date-only expense timing cannot support a stabilization-time expense boundary.
findings.issue: ExpenseLine has only service_on:date. The excluded-provider exception case requires allocating expenses before versus after a specific stabilization instant. Episode-wide start/end and a clinical assertion do not locate individual room/procedure charges within that boundary. A single bill line may also span the boundary.
findings.required_revision: Represent expense service instants/intervals and precision, with an explicit original-backed allocation for lines spanning a boundary. Preserve date-only unknown precision without inventing midnight. Link the authoritative clinical stabilization event and any approved allocation assumption to the calculation.

findings.title: Hospital observations omit decisive accessibility, clinician and observation-completeness dimensions.
findings.issue: ProviderObservation.status is network/nonnetwork/restricted/excluded/unknown, while the cases independently require wheelchair accessibility, participation of a named specialist, authorization and whether a negative directory search was complete. Provider is a facility branch, and ProviderScopeV1 contains only services/network tier/territories/scope status. A generic services string cannot express the independently dated boolean/unknown observation, clinician identity or search completeness without an unspecified convention.
findings.required_revision: Add a typed observation kind/value and relevant subject identities/provenance, or another explicit representation covering each independent requirement. Keep non-network and excluded state separately observable, and retain query coverage so a missing hit cannot become a verified negative.

findings.title: Mixed/private uniqueness is not consistently scoped to ownership.
findings.issue: Rule is mixed/private but unique(terms_id,rule_key,revision) omits owner_id. Two customers with different private versions of the same logical rule collide, including terms_id NULL because NULLS NOT DISTINCT is requested. SearchChunk uniqueness likewise omits owner despite mixed/private use; identical scoped derivatives need an explicit sharing/deduplication policy.
findings.required_revision: Separate public and private rule namespaces or include the appropriate scope/owner key in uniqueness. Define whether private chunks can reference shared public sources and whether equal derivatives are separate owner records; ensure uniqueness errors cannot couple independent customer state.

findings.title: Unknown waiting/credit durations cannot be represented by the required duration type.
findings.issue: DurationV1 requires a nonnegative integer value, unit, anchor and boundary, with no unknown variant. ContinuityCredit.period is required even when the credit is pending/unmeasured, and a waiting effect requires DurationV1 directly. The broader design promises unknown distinct from zero; a placeholder zero or omitted pending record would lose that distinction.
findings.required_revision: Provide a tagged unknown/unresolved duration or a distinct pending-credit representation, and specify how unknown trigger/boundary propagates. Do not fabricate zero months or a credit anchor to satisfy a required shape. Confirm absolute caps and waits without a credit also have non-invented ways to represent inapplicable percentage/credit inputs.

findings.title: Named strict JSON shapes still need explicit semantic validators and event-specific requirements.
findings.issue: With Draft202012Validator and a FormatChecker, invalid interval strings pass TemporalExtentV1; five repeated family dimensions pass ReconciliationV1; a decision event without decision_id passes TurnEventV1; and a one-argument divide passes ExpressionV1. AdditionalProperties=false does not establish these invariants. Table selector axis uniqueness/range composition also remains a prose obligation.
findings.required_revision: Tighten shapes where feasible and enumerate mandatory semantic validation gates for parsing/chronology, exactly-once reconciliation dimensions, AST arity/units/depth, event-kind required fields and axis/range completeness. Persist validator versions and prevent publication/indexing until these checks pass. These findings do not imply schema-invalid JSON itself.

findings.title: Delete/update actions and erasure transitions are not yet specified for the relationships.
findings.issue: The field dictionary describes FK targets and purposes but does not provide a complete on_delete/on_update/deferred constraint contract. Account erasure, reviewer retention and immutable source/citation graphs require different actions. A default CASCADE or a broad PROTECT can respectively erase retained evidence or make authorized deletion impossible.
findings.required_revision: Specify every relationship deletion/update action, nullability transition and deferral requirement, including reviewer identity minimization and retained public originals. Demonstrate a selective erasure and an account purge against those exact constraints before calling the proposed migration design complete.

findings.title: Package/subsumed expense relationships are not structurally represented.
findings.issue: The cases require distinguishing separately payable lines, excluded items and supplies already included in a room/procedure package. ExpenseLine has a category and relation-to-hospitalisation assertion but no package parent, included-line relationship or explicit allocation grouping. A text label cannot prevent counting an implant or consumable both as a package component and a separate allowance.
findings.required_revision: Specify the typed package/inclusion/allocation relation and its provenance, including whether inclusion affects billing, admissibility, cap membership or all three. Validate cycles and duplicate allocation and expose the membership used by calculation traces.

schema_only_counterexamples_accepted: invalid date strings in an interval

positive_findings: Proposal and user-approval boundary are explicitly marked; no model or migration implementation is claimed.
Encoded passwords are explicitly preserved without rehashing, and native session layout is retained.
Original hashes, immutable fact snapshots, exact rule/evidence links, durable turn events and distinct failure outcomes are represented.
Threshold contribution, cover consumption and actual payment are separate fields; unknown quantities are distinct from zero for QuantityV1.
RuleTable/RuleTableCell retain axis selectors, cell evidence and connected footnotes.
Public BM25 versus PostgreSQL text-search fallback and private prefiltering are explicitly distinguished.
approval_boundary: These are required proposal revisions for discussion, not authorization to implement schema changes. Full derivation from all 400 independently assessed cases remains outside this source-structure check.
verification_limit: No Django check, migrations, database connections, service calls or actual customer/authentication rows were used; this is a source/JSON design review with isolated jsonschema probes. It does not establish runtime database enforcement or compatibility.
